title: Recurrent patterns of TOP1-mediated neuronal genomic damage shared by major neurodegenerative disorders.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.20174164 (via its API): software only, one code zip of the GitHub repo parklab/zhou_luquette_2026_genomic_damage_in_neurodegeneration (CC-BY-4.0). Listed the repo: R/Python analysis scripts, COSMIC signature reference, a 3 KB DNA-break quantification CSV and a 1 KB post-mortem-interval CSV; no mutation-call tables. The analysis README says inputs are SCAN2 (a single-cell mutation caller) summary objects that are not in the repo. The two Mendeley DOIs in the text-mined accessions returned 404. Europe PMC full text and supplement returned HTTP 500 or nothing; the PMC page was blocked by a CAPTCHA.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 469 neurons, the disease groups and the ID4-like indel fractions come from the abstract. Controlled access comes from the preprint (PMC11908196) data statement: 'Sequencing data generated in this study will be deposited in a public repository, with controlled use conditions set by human privacy regulations'; previously published data came from dbGaP and NIAGADS. I could not see the final Cell data statement.

a1_downloadable.note: The raw single-cell whole-genome sequencing data is human brain data under controlled access (dbGaP/NIAGADS-style application, per the preprint). Only code is openly downloadable, and the per-neuron mutation tables (Cell supplementary tables) could not be retrieved.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files. The obvious label (donor disease status) would sit in a metadata table that isn't public in the repo, and the main features (mutational signature exposures) would have to be rebuilt from mutation calls.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not in any public file I could open. The repo needs SCAN2 summary objects that come from controlled-access BAM files (aligned sequencing reads).

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked. Mutation burdens are counts per genome, which is unambiguous.

a5_enough_rows.note: 469 neurons (abstract only), but the independent unit is the donor: about 6 ALS, 6 FTD, a handful of AD and the controls. That is far too few donors for honest held-out evaluation.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; mutation tables would be MB-scale
a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw BAMs would be terabytes, but processed mutation calls would fit easily.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Can't check: no public data table could be opened.

a8_label_provenance.note: Disease status comes from neuropathology diagnosis, not from a model. But the signature exposures are themselves fitted from the mutation calls.

backbone.name: none applicable (the features would be mutation counts per neuron)

integration.partner_dataset: COSMIC mutational signatures; earlier Walsh/Park-lab neuron single-cell sequencing datasets (aging neurons, CTE (chronic traumatic encephalopathy)), also controlled access
integration.join_key: none at row level (signature names only)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Is a TOP1-linked indel signature a shared marker of neuronal damage across neurodegenerative diseases and CTE? This is answerable only with controlled-access data from many donors.

controls.positive_control: Mutation burden that rises with age in control neurons (a known effect)
controls.external_validation: CTE single-neuron sequencing (Dong et al., Science), also controlled access

honest_claim_h3: With about 20 donors, a model could at most say that neurons from these few brains carrying this indel signature tend to come from diseased donors, not that it diagnoses disease.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the mutation patterns in single brain neurons to predict whether the donor had ALS, frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease or no disease.
plain_idea.train_on: Counts of each mutation type per neuron for 469 neurons (number from the paper; no public table found), from roughly 20–30 donors.
plain_idea.predict: The donor's diagnosis, made by neuropathology at autopsy.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would test whether DNA damage patterns separate the diseases. But the paper already shows this by simple signature fractions, and the donor count is too small for machine learning to add anything.

label_elsewhere.sources: Not scored for a reject. Other single-neuron sequencing studies exist but are controlled access.

ml_idea: Classify neuron or donor disease status from indel and single-base mutation spectra, then test transfer to CTE neurons. It is blocked by controlled access and by about 20 donors.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no public data table exists to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether Cell's supplementary tables list per-neuron mutation calls with donor IDs, and count the donors. It is already dead on A1 for the raw data.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 and A5: the brain single-cell sequencing data is controlled access (preprint data statement), and the open Zenodo/GitHub deposit is code only. On top of that, the 469 neurons come from only about 20 donors, too few for a held-out evaluation.
